0.0.n: Adds a casual, friendly opening to the greeting.

0.1.n: さん makes this way of addressing the audience polite.

0.2.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

0.4.n: This is the speaker’s name or nickname.

0.5.n: Politely completes the introduction; the speaker leaves out 私は.

1.0.n: Describes the viewers’ regular support, not just this particular viewing.

1.1.n: Japanese does not mark plural here; the speaker means their videos.

1.2.n: Marks 動画 as what the viewers watch.

1.3.n: 見る in て-form plus humble いただく presents viewers’ watching as a favor; いただき connects to the thanks.

1.5.n: Combines with ございます to make the thanks polite.

1.6.n: ござい is part of ございます, which adds formality to ありがとう.

1.7.n: Completes ございます; it does not indicate a separate action here.

2.0.n: Introduces the subject of this particular video.

2.1.n: Marks 今回 as the topic of the short announcement.

2.2.n: Politely points to the item being presented; です is left unstated.

3.0.n: Refers to a recent day without specifying the date.

3.1.n: Past form of 発売する directly describes iPhone 17; it is not grammatically passive despite the natural English translation.

3.2.n: This is Apple’s product name, followed by the model number.

3.4.n: Identifies the iPhone model rather than a quantity.

4.0.n: Refers back to the iPhone 17 being shown.

4.1.n: Marks こちら as the thing that arrived.

4.2.n: Polite past form of 届く, used when a delivery reaches its destination.

4.3.n: Connects the arrival to the reason for starting the review.

4.4.n: Signals starting without delay now that the phone has arrived.

4.5.n: Means opening packaging and combines with レビュー to name the type of review.

4.6.n: レビューする + ていく + たい expresses wanting to proceed with the review.

4.7.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

4.8.n: Polite form of 思う; following たいと, it gently announces what the speaker wants to do.

5.0.n: Links the new information to the previous introduction.

5.1.n: Sets the time frame for the phone currently in use.

5.2.n: A personal pronoun commonly used by male speakers, less formal than 私.

5.3.n: Marks 僕 as the topic, introducing the speaker’s own situation.

5.4.n: Points to the iPhone 16 being shown.

5.5.n: Links こちら to iPhone 16, forming a polite way to say this iPhone 16.

5.8.n: Specifies the model of the speaker’s current phone.

5.9.n: Marks the iPhone 16 as what the speaker uses.

5.10.n: 使う in て-form plus います politely describes ongoing use, not necessarily use at this exact second.

6.0.n: Frames the switch being discussed as the speaker’s latest upgrade.

6.1.n: Short for iPhone 16; the product name is omitted.

6.2.n: Marks the old model as the starting point of the switch.

6.3.n: Short for iPhone 17, the new model.

6.4.n: Marks the destination of the switch; this particle is pronounced え.

6.5.n: Past form of 乗り換える, describing 理由; here it means changing devices rather than transferring trains.

6.6.n: The preceding phrase explains what these reasons are for.

6.7.n: Makes the reasons sound like one example among related topics, keeping the tone casual.

6.8.n: Adds discussing the reasons to the planned unboxing review.

6.9.n: お話しする is a polite way to say talk; していこう expresses an intention to proceed.

6.10.n: Combines with な to express gentle self-questioning rather than asking the audience.

6.11.n: Completes かな, making the proposed plan sound relaxed and tentative.

6.12.n: Marks the preceding tentative plan as the content of 思います.

6.13.n: Politely closes the sentence; with かなと, it presents an intention softly.

0.tip: Japanese introductions often omit I and simply use a name followed by です.

1.lit: Always, receiving the favor of watching videos, thank you.
1.tip: 見ていただき respectfully treats the audience’s watching as a favor received by the speaker.

2.tip: こちら can politely point to an object, not just a direction or person.

3.tip: Japanese places descriptions like 先日発売した directly before the noun they describe.

4.lit: This arrived, so right away an unboxing review I want to proceed with, I think.
4.tip: たいと思います is a common, gentle way to announce what you intend to do.

5.lit: And now, as for me, this iPhone 16 am using.
5.tip: 使っています describes the speaker’s current ongoing use of this phone.

6.lit: This time, reasons for switching from 16 to 17 and such also, shall I talk about, I wonder, I think.
6.tip: かなと思います softens a plan into something like I think I’ll do that.
